title: Matched before-count subtraction retained a larger deep-event late share at 200 km in ComCat for 2001-2024
abstract: We tested whether nearby before-event counts explain a reported deep-minus-shallow late-share contrast. We reused a fixed ComCat snapshot, with 646 shallow and 99 deep M6.5 to below 8 centers in 2001-2024 and M5.5 or larger neighbors within a 200 km chord. Matched before-count subtraction gave late shares of 63.57% and 24.00%. The difference was 39.57 percentage points, with conditional 95% three-year block limits of 18.10 to 64.25. A test without division by corrected totals gave C=0.04818, with limits 0.01914 to 0.08448. All main draws had positive corrected totals. This adds uncertainty tests to previously reported corrected point values. It is not independent confirmation. The C interval included zero at 100 km and without center isolation. A remote-before correction also depended on block length. Before subtraction therefore retained the contrast at the main settings, but did not establish a general depth effect or slower physical recovery. Sparse counts, regional dependence, selection, source revision and background assumptions limit inference. Original code, aggregate counts, draws, an independent recount and offline reproduction checks are included. Source records stay external.

display.caption: Count-shape contrast C and total counts after two background corrections. Bars show conditional 95% three-year block limits. C orders the two late shares when both corrected totals are positive.

citations.reason: We reuse its cohort and standardization on the same source snapshot. It already reports corrected point shares. We add denominator-free uncertainty and remote-background tests.
Its isolation sensitivity motivates care with before-event controls.
